title: Learn-by-Compare: Analog Performance Prediction using Contrastive Regression with Design Knowledge
problem: Accurate analog circuit performance prediction from design parameters is computationally expensive using traditional simulation methods. Existing regression approaches struggle to capture complex nonlinear relationships in analog circuit behavior.
motivation: Efficient and accurate analog performance modeling accelerates circuit design iteration and enables automated design space exploration.
method: The system trains a deep neural network to predict analog circuit performance by comparing different designs and learning which ones perform similarly or differently—this comparison-based learning is called contrastive regression. To work with limited labeled examples, it learns from both labeled and unlabeled data together (semi-supervised learning). It creates synthetic training examples at two levels to maximize the usefulness of each real example: first by varying individual transistor sizes (transistor-level augmentation, or LS-DA), then by adjusting overall circuit configuration (global sizing augmentation, or GS-DA), guided by knowledge of how circuits actually work.
key_novelty: The core idea combines semi-supervised contrastive regression (learning by comparing circuit designs, using both labeled and unlabeled data) with hierarchical data augmentation at the transistor (LS-DA) and global (GS-DA) levels, using design knowledge to efficiently predict analog circuit performance.
contributions: Contrastive regression framework for learning accurate analog circuit performance predictors
Two-level hierarchical data augmentation strategy (LS-DA and GS-DA) leveraging circuit design knowledge
Semi-supervised learning approach reducing reliance on extensively labeled circuit data
Superior predictive accuracy demonstrated over traditional regression methods
